title: Token Mix Fairshare: HC Rotation & Price Trigger Lab
content:
Purpose:
This workbook is an experimental sandbox for: (1) mapping rolling headcount tranches into a fairshare token allocation model, (2) modelling price-floor triggers when token run-rate crosses stress thresholds, and (3) producing quick sensitivity outputs for exec decisioning. This is intentionally simple — intended to be converted into the canonical run-rate simulator if results hold.

Key assumptions (baseline):
- Baseline month (M0) billable token mix = 65% chat-gen, 20% embeddings, 15% rerank/other.
- Baseline price/revenue per 1k tokens (weighted average) = $0.024.
- HC cost per FTE (fully loaded average finance model) = $230k/year -> ~$19.2k/month.
- Dedicated GPU capacity reserve cost bucket = $120k/month (committed).
- Elasticity assumptions (for quick stress): chat elasticity = -0.20, embeddings = -0.04, rerank = -0.12 for price changes near +/-10%.

Sheet 1 — HC rotation tranches (monthly):
Columns: Tranche, Start Month, Role Mix, FTEs, Monthly Cost, Notes
- Tranche A | M0 | Eng Ops 40% / SRE 30% / Finance 10% / Sales 20% | 12 FTE | $230k/month | immediate hires for Q4 launch support
- Tranche B | M2 | Serving eng 60% / Infra 20% / Support 20% | 8 FTE | $153.6k/month | scale capacity engineering
- Tranche C | M5 | Sales & RevOps 80% / CS 20% | 6 FTE | $115.2k/month | GTM expansion batch
Formula notes: Monthly Cost = FTEs * (HC cost per FTE / 12) rounded to nearest $100.

Sheet 2 — Fairshare token allocator (concept):
Inputs: active customers, historic 90-day consumption, committed throughput commitments.
Algorithm (high level):
1) Compute 90d median usage per customer (tokens/day).
2) Assign fairshare weight = committed tier weight + (90d median / total 90d median) * dynamic band (0–1).
3) Compute theoretical capacity share = fairshare weight / sum(weights).
4) Map capacity share into token budget by capacity pool.
This is important because HC rotation impacts capacity pools (Dedicated vs Hosted) and therefore the unit economics per token.

Sheet 3 — Price trigger matrix (operational rules):
Triggers are expressed as% run-rate delta over 7d median.
- Soft trigger (>= +15% 7d median vs baseline): dispatch PRicingOps to increase price floor by +4% and enable temporary burst pool (30% capacity) funded from reserve.
- Hard trigger (>= +40% 7d median): escalate to Finance + Sales; recommend +12% price floor, restrict new free-tier signups, and allocate immediate tranche B hires (if not already active).
- Tail-risk down (<= -25% sustained 30d): initiate HC rotation pause (defer Tranche C); propose 8% promo credits to retain top 10% of customers by revenue.
Trigger rationale: prefer price-floor nudges before immediate HC decisions; HC rotation is last-resort for downside.

Sheet 4 — Sensitivity summary (snapshot outputs):
Scenario definitions:
- Base = current run-rate, current mix.
- High-demand = +30% run-rate, mix shifts +10pp to chat (chat-heavy).
- Compression = -20% run-rate, weighted move to embeddings.

Quick outputs (rounded):
1) Base: monthly revenue = $3.6M, gross margin (before HC) = 43%.
2) High-demand (no price change): revenue = $4.68M, infra cost up 22% (due to peak utilization), gross margin = 38% -> recommended price-floor +6% leads to revenue $4.96M and margin = 41% (considers elasticity).
3) Compression: revenue = $2.88M, margin = 31%.
Tradeoffs: adding Tranche B early (M1 vs M2) increases SRE/serving capacity reducing infra overspill by ~70% in High-demand scenario but increases fixed HC burn by +\$153.6k/month. Payback if incremental revenue > 5 months for that tranche.

Sheet 5 — Short-run staffing hedges (playbook snippet):
- Immediate: maintain hiring freeze on non-customer-facing roles when 30d revenue delta <= -10%.
- Conditional burst hires: convert 2 contractor slots to perm if High-demand trigger persists for 45d and price-floor adjustments already applied.
- Reallocation: shift 1 supporting infra engineer from internal tools to capacity reliability where required (temporary 3-month secondment).

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Validate elasticity assumptions with Product pricing team (particularly embeddings elasticity).
- Approve reservoir for temporary burst pool funding: can we earmark 20% of reserve bucket to a rapid response pool?
- Legal check: any constraints on tier changes that would require customer notice >30 days?

Appendix — quick sensitivity table (excerpt):
Price change vs revenue change (approx):
- Price +5% => revenue +3.5% (mix-weighted elasticities)
- Price +10% => revenue +6.8%
- Price -10% => revenue -12% (chat-sensitive)

Next steps (owner tags):
- Finance (Leah) => bake these scenarios into canonical run-rate simulator (due 2026-11-30).
- Product (Mina) => sanity-check embeddings elasticity (due 2026-11-18).
- Eng Ops (Jordan) => confirm realistic lead times for Tranche B hires (due 2026-11-20).

Notes to reviewer: this sheet is intentionally experimental. The fairshare allocation described is a heuristic — if we want to operationalize, we should simulate at customer-level for last 180 days and run mildew tests (stress outs).

Signed: Leah M. (Finance) — draft for cross-team review
